1.15.2.0 predates the current naming scheme. The Slingshot stamp sits inside the package name itself, _SSHOT2.1.3. It does not sit in the release field, the way 2.3.1’s SHS13.1.0 does. 2.3.1 is the only one of the three with the modern layout. In this layout, rpm -q reports version and release as separate fields, and the package name stays plain libfabric. No RPM owns 1.22.0. It is the host case: a file placed on the host outside the RPM database. So rpm -qf on anything under that tree returns empty.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text: libfabric reads the FI_* family, including the CXI-specific FI_CXI_* variables. Environment variables lists this family. FI_MR_CACHE_MONITOR and FI_CXI_RX_MATCH_MODE are frequent diagnostic targets.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• libcxi is the user-space library that the CXI provider calls.
  • cxi-driver is the kernel driver underneath.
  • cassini-headers provides the build-time headers for the CXI provider.
  • aws-ofi-nccl routes NCCL traffic over this library.

docs.title: mpich
docs.text:
MPICH is the reference implementation of the MPI standard. Cray MPICH derives from MPICH and is ABI-compatible with it.

Property Value Spack package mpich Layer MPI Provided by User. User-buildable Yes. Slingshot component Indirectly, through libfabric with the ch4:ofi device. Upstream https://www.mpich.org

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
MPICH is relevant to the netstack for two reasons.

ABI compatibility Cray MPICH implements the MPICH 3.4a2 ABI. A binary built against upstream mpich can run against Cray MPICH. A binary built against Cray MPICH can also run against upstream mpich. This is why user-stack reports the role as “ABI-compatible MPICH”. An alternative MPI You can build mpich with the ch4:ofi device against libfabric and the CXI provider. You can then run it over Slingshot without Cray MPICH. On Alps, the Cray build has better fabric tuning, so it is the default choice.

docs.title: System or user
docs.text:
When it is present, mpich is always a user component.

The prgenv-gnu uenvs use Cray MPICH rather than upstream mpich. This page documents the package for completeness, and for environments that choose it.

docs.title: Identifying it
docs.text:
mpichversion distinguishes the two builds. A Cray build reports Cray-specific configure flags and a GTL-built-with custom string. A plain build does not report these.

If the MPI library resolves to a Spack store directory named mpich-* rather than cray-mpich-*, it is upstream MPICH.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• cray-mpich is the Cray-tuned derivative, and the default on Alps.
  • openmpi is the other MPI family.
  • libfabric is the fabric that a ch4:ofi build runs over.

docs.title: nccl
docs.text:
NCCL is NVIDIA’s collective communication library. Applications use it for multi-GPU and multi-node reductions, broadcasts and all-gathers.

Property Value Spack package nccl Layer GPU collectives Provided by User. User-buildable Yes. Slingshot component Indirectly, through aws-ofi-nccl and libfabric. Upstream https://github.com/NVIDIA/nccl

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: NCCL, as libnccl.so.2, implements optimized primitives for collective communication between GPUs. Inside a node it uses NVLink and PCIe directly. Across nodes, it needs a network transport plugin. On Alps, that plugin is aws-ofi-nccl. It carries NCCL traffic over libfabric and the CXI provider. NCCL and MPI therefore share the same Slingshot fabric.

docs.title: System or user
docs.text: NCCL is always a user component. It ships in the uenv, in a container, or in a pip wheel. It sits on the view path. It links the CUDA runtime.

docs.title: Identifying it
docs.text:
The soname carries the full release. user-stack reads the version from it directly.

Environment Version prgenv-gnu/25.11:v1 2.28.3 prgenv-gnu/25.6:v2 2.27.5 prgenv-gnu/24.7:v3 2.20.3

libnccl.so.2.<major>.<minor> gives the version. The NCCL_MAJOR, NCCL_MINOR and NCCL_PATCH macros in nccl.h confirm it.

Check that the fabric path is wired up

With NCCL_DEBUG=INFO, NCCL prints the network plugin it selected at startup. This is the fastest way to confirm that traffic goes over the fabric and not a fallback.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text: NCCL reads the NCCL_* family of variables. See Environment variables for the full list. For the netstack, the important variables are NCCL_NET_PLUGIN, NCCL_NET and NCCL_DEBUG. NCCL_NET_PLUGIN selects aws-ofi-nccl.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• aws-ofi-nccl is the libfabric and CXI transport plugin.
  • libfabric is the fabric that NCCL ultimately runs over.
  • cuda provides the runtime that NCCL links.

docs.title: openmpi
docs.text:
Open MPI is an alternative MPI implementation. It also runs over libfabric and the CXI provider on Slingshot.

Property Value Spack package openmpi Layer MPI Provided by User. User-buildable Yes. Slingshot component Indirectly, through libfabric and the OFI MTL or BTL. Upstream https://www.open-mpi.org

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
Open MPI is an independent, community-developed MPI implementation. On Alps, it reaches Slingshot through its OFI component. This is the same libfabric cxi provider that Cray MPICH uses.

Dedicated environments such as prgenv-gnu-openmpi package Open MPI. The standard prgenv-gnu uses Cray MPICH instead.

Open MPI is not ABI-compatible with MPICH

mpich and cray-mpich share an ABI. Open MPI does not share this ABI. An application must be built and run against the same MPI family as Open MPI.

docs.title: System or user
docs.text:
Open MPI is always a user component.

Its netstack dependencies are libfabric, libcxi, xpmem and cuda. These follow the same system or user rules as they do for Cray MPICH. Check their provenance per environment with the tools.

docs.title: Identifying it
docs.text:
user-stack is aware of the MPI flavour. It resolves the MPI library to its Spack store directory. This distinguishes openmpi-* from cray-mpich-* and mpich-*. It reports the matching implementation. For an Open MPI stack, it emits an openmpi row. The version comes from ompi_info --version. In place of the Cray-specific cray-gtl, cray-pmi and cray-pals rows, it emits a pmix row.

Output for prgenv-gnu-openmpi/26.3:v1

Component Version Origin Role openmpi 5.0.10 uenv MPI (Open MPI) libfabric 2.3.1 uenv OFI fabric abstraction libcxi 1.5.0 uenv Slingshot (CXI) user-space library nccl 2.29.2 uenv GPU collectives aws-ofi-nccl 1.17.2 uenv NCCL to libfabric transport plugin cuda 13.1.1 uenv CUDA runtime (toolkit) pmix 2.13.10 uenv Process management interface (PMIx)

Two other signs identify it. The MPI library is libmpi.so.40 for Open MPI, rather than libmpi_*.so.12 for Cray MPICH. ompi_info also lists the MCA components. Look for the ofi MTL or BTL. This component is Slingshot through libfabric. Also look for the cuda accelerator. This component gives GPU-awareness without a GTL.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text: OMPI_* variables and MCA parameters configure Open MPI, not MPICH_* variables. PMIX_* variables configure its launch. The fabric-level FI_* variables still apply. Environment variables lists all three families.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• cray-mpich and mpich are the MPICH family.
  • pmix is the launch and wire-up interface that Open MPI uses.
  • libfabric is the fabric layer shared with Cray MPICH.

docs.title: pmix
docs.text:
PMIx, the Process Management Interface for Exascale, is the launch and wire-up interface that Open MPI uses. It is the counterpart to Cray MPICH’s cray-pmi.

Property Value Spack package pmix, often bundled inside openmpi. Layer Launch and wire-up Provided by User. User-buildable Yes. Slingshot component No. Upstream https://openpmix.github.io/

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
PMIx, as libpmix.so, is the successor to PMI and PMI-2. It is the interface that an MPI runtime uses to bootstrap a job. Before the fabric can carry any traffic, PMIx publishes and exchanges connection data, discovers ranks, and coordinates with the launcher. It is the control-plane counterpart to the data plane. libfabric and XPMEM make up the data plane.

At run time, PMIx connects to the PMIx server of the launcher. For srun --mpi=pmix, this is the server embedded in Slurm. For mpirun, this is the server in Open MPI’s own PRRTE.

docs.title: System or user
docs.text: PMIx is a user component. In prgenv-gnu-openmpi, it ships inside the Open MPI package. libpmix.so.2 lives in the openmpi-* store prefix. Because of this, user-stack attributes it to the Spack hash of Open MPI. You can also install it as a standalone pmix package.

docs.title: Identifying it
docs.text:
user-stack reports pmix whenever libpmix.so is on the view path. This is the signal that the MPI stack uses PMIx rather than Cray PMI.

Environment Version (soname) Origin prgenv-gnu-openmpi/26.3:v1 2.13.10 uenv

As with libcxi, the soname version, from libpmix.so.2.13.10, is the shared-object version. It differs from the PMIx release number. See version namespaces.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text: The launcher populates most of the PMIX_* family. It covers the server URI, the rank and the namespace. Environment variables lists it.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• openmpi is the MPI that uses PMIx here.
  • cray-pmi is the Cray MPICH equivalent.
  • slurm provides a PMIx server for srun.

docs.title: slurm
docs.text:
Slurm is the workload manager. In the netstack it matters as a launcher, because srun starts the ranks and provides the PMI wire-up.

Property Value Spack package slurm Layer Launch Provided by System. User-buildable No. The site manages it. Slingshot component No. Upstream https://slurm.schedmd.com/

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
Slurm schedules jobs and, through srun, launches the processes of a parallel job. Its relevant job for the netstack is process management. srun places ranks on nodes. srun also speaks PMI and PMI-2 to bootstrap MPI. It exchanges the information each rank needs before the ranks can use the fabric. It is one of the two launch paths on Alps. The other is cray-pals under mpiexec.

Slurm does not move application data. That is the job of the fabric: libfabric and XPMEM. Slurm matters here because a wire-up that uses the wrong PMI, or a mismatched PMI, causes a genuine netstack failure.

docs.title: System or user
docs.text: Slurm is always a system component. The site installs and manages it. The RPM is slurm, version 25.5.4 on the reference node. system-stack reports it.

docs.title: Identifying it
docs.text:
SLURM_* environment variables in a job show that Slurm launched it.

Listing the PMI plugins that Slurm can provide
$ srun --mpi=list

system-stack reports the installed Slurm version.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• cray-pmi provides the PMI libraries that the launcher drives.
  • pmix is the PMIx interface that Slurm can also serve.
  • cray-pals is the alternative, Cray, launcher.

docs.title: xpmem
docs.text:
XPMEM is a Linux kernel module for intra-node shared memory. It lets one process map another’s address space. This enables single-copy MPI transfers within a node.

Property Value Spack package xpmem Layer Intra-node shared memory Provided by System, as a kernel module. Users can build the userspace library. User-buildable The userspace library yes, the kernel module no, because it must match the host. Slingshot component No. Upstream https://github.com/hpc/xpmem

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
XPMEM lets a process map the memory of another process into its own virtual address space. Cray MPICH uses it as the single-copy transport for large intra-node messages. Set MPICH_SMP_SINGLE_COPY_MODE=XPMEM to select it. This avoids the double copy through a shared-memory buffer. It is the intra-node counterpart to the fabric. Traffic that stays on a node goes through XPMEM. Traffic that leaves a node goes through libfabric.

Like the CXI driver, XPMEM has a kernel-module half that matches the running kernel. You cannot replace this half from user space. The userspace libxpmem.so is a thin shim over it.

docs.title: System or user
docs.text: XPMEM is a system component. On Alps, the module and libxpmem.so come from the host at /opt/xpmem. They come from the RPMs xpmem and cray-libxpmem-devel, version 1.0.1. user-stack resolves libxpmem.so to the host in all reference uenvs. It finds this through ld.so.conf.

docs.title: Identifying it
docs.text:
system-stack reports xpmem version 1.0.1 from the RPM, with prefix /opt/xpmem. user-stack reports the same 1.0.1. It shows an rpm origin, with ld.so.conf as the search mechanism that found it.

The version comes from the RPM, not the file

The host libxpmem.so has the soname 0.0.0. This is an uninformative libtool soname. It carries no real version. user-stack asks the RPM database which package owns the file it resolved. It reports the version from there instead.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text: MPICH_SMP_SINGLE_COPY_MODE selects XPMEM, as opposed to CMA or NONE. Environment variables lists it.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• cray-mpich is the main consumer of XPMEM.
  • libfabric is the off-node counterpart.
  • cxi-driver is the other host kernel-module component.
